title: Dispatches of A. W. C. van Reede from Berlin to L. P. van de Spiegel, 1787-1788, in William V's Grand Chiffre (DECODE R1026, R1027)

steps.what: Used the existing private DECODE cookie to download the record metadata, transcriptions and manuscript images of R1026, R1027 (and R1893, now vanreede1793).
Normalized the DECODE J-like glyph as handwritten digit 3 in R1026 and R1027 and extracted numerical groups.
Compared R1026 and R1027 group inventories; they share 49 groups and therefore use the same code system.
Separated R1893 as a different system because its three-digit groups carry systematic per-digit marks absent from the earlier dispatches.
Located Karl de Leeuw's account of Dutch diplomatic code practice and the Nationaal Archief catalogue entry for Van Nagell's 1787 code (current inv. 28).
Decoded the R1028 control (plaintext on DECODE) with key R1024.
Decoded R1026/R1027 with R1024 treating J+ as 3; groups containing J+ read as nonsense.
Resolved each J+ as any digit by beam search with a French 6-gram model (hellen1752 corpus); 105 groups resolved, both letters read.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from vanreede1787, which had joined R1026/R1027 (William V's 1782 Grand Chiffre, R1024) with R1893 (1793, a different marked three-digit code). This profile keeps R1026 and R1027 (Grand Chiffre) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R1026 and R1027 linked to the DECODE group transcriptions, the J+-resolved group files (resolve_j.py) and the readings with the Grand Chiffre R1024

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): reading_R1026.txt and reading_R1027.txt read through; a few sentences read, but garbled runs from DECODE digit misreads and open codes break most of them (docs/_check_reading.py 73% and 57% clean, inflated by code words that are dictionary forms). Both relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved; fraction_read 0.949 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b24): DECODE R1026 and R1027 fetched again with the shared cookie (b24_fetch.py, scratchpad): only the page images and the transcription; no attachment, comment or decipherment on either record. The printed Van de Spiegel correspondence already in the main checkout (Brieven en negotiatien i-iii, Vreede's Van de Spiegel iii) has no Van Reede letter of these dates; no contemporary decipherment or copy.

DECODE's 'J+' looked at on zoomed strips of the letters: it is one glyph, the writer's 1 with a hooked foot (the plain 1 also occurs). J=1 gives a key word that fits at every occurrence (77 in R1026, 24 in R1027: 'au Roi le projet', 'à dix heures', 'il n'y a', 'la reponse est arrivée'); J=3 gives 'au reste il n'est le projet', and the 21 Sept beam search had chosen 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 per group, the source of the garble.

Key R1024 checked on its images where its DECODE transcription has holes: the missing ranges 1-50, 331-370, 1201-1250, 2751-2800, 3131-3160 and 3621-3660 are blocks headed 'Nonvaleurs depuis ... jusqu'à ...' (nulls), which accounts for the 'open codes' 1250, 331, 2800, 3160, 3660, 3153, 2751, 50, 1201; number-column slips fixed by page order (3637 'cependant' = 2637, 3635 = 2635, 1615 = 2615, 2520 = 2530, 3530 = 3539, 3577 = 3677, 3230 = 3730); word slips read on the images: 54 est (not es), 2142 paroit, 2143 paroitre (missing), 4910 que (not quo) (b24_vr_key.py). Each holds at every occurrence in R1026/R1027.

Every group of R1027 and the flagged groups of R1026 re-read on zoomed strips of the DECODE images (b24_strips.py): R1026 '1?00' = 100, '21423068' = 2142 3068, '4 4 3 8' = 4438 corrected by the writer to 4433, '51?' = 513 (flat-backed 3), '308?9' = 3089; R1027 '3?089' = 3089, '1?1021' = 1021, '0969' = 1969; the rest of DECODE's digits confirmed (R1026_corrections.tsv, R1027_corrections.tsv, *_transcription_corrected.tsv).

The bar marks over and under groups are the code's inflection signs: a bar above cuts final letters from the key word (prier = prié, soin + R = soir, motif + ver = motiver, Sieur + N = sien, entendre = entend, temperer + or air E = temporaire, laissai + nt = laissant, seulement = seule; over the first digit it cuts the front: 'le Comtte de Finkenstein' = Comtte de Finkenstein), a bar below adds the ending (Ministres, heures, possessions, Puissances, a faite, connue); an accent stroke gives é (entrées, decidé). No instruction sheet on the record; read from the letters only.

Readings written on the figures (R1026_reading.md, R1027_reading.md; translations R1026_en.md, R1027_en.md); the clear passages of R1026 read from the image (DECODE's cleartext lines are garbled). Word check (b24_vr_align.py): every word of the cipher parts is in the decoded stream or explained by a bar mark. _check_reading.py on the bodies: R1026 0.735 (25/34), R1027 0.867 (13/15); explicit-hole share 0.971 and 0.933; before 0.00 (audit). Both set read, grade B (bar-mark convention inferred, not documented).

R1893 decoded with Van Reede's 1789-92 marked code to Wilhelmina (target reede1789, rebuilt from KHA A32-545-547 interlinear glosses): 40% coverage at chance level, French values in a Dutch letter; R1893 marks sit above digits. Not this code.

outcome.method_basis: William V's 1782 Grand Chiffre (DECODE R1024, named on the DECODE records) reads R1026 and R1027 once DECODE's J+ sign is taken as the writer's hooked 1 and the key's null blocks and transcription slips are read off the key images (b24, 23 Oct 2026); R1028's DECODE plaintext served as control.

gaps.item: R1026 [?soit], [?fournit], [?énonçoit]; R1027 [?decidement]: four words where the groups and their bar marks spell a slip ('soient' + bars, 'E Nonce ois', 'de ci demi ent')
gaps.detail: the key carries no instruction for the bar marks; the reading is the sense the groups point to

gaps.item: R1026 clear passage: 'je [?vois] le plus [?estimé] d'[?ici]', 'le jour [?la]'
gaps.detail: faint hand on the 1240-px DECODE image; a better image of NA 3.01.26 inv. 190 would settle them

outcome.notes: R1026 and R1027 read with William V's Grand Chiffre (R1024). Split 14 Oct 2026: R1893 is vanreede1793. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: both relabelled decoded, not read (garbled runs). 23 Oct 2026 (b24): the garble came from resolving DECODE's J+ sign digit by digit with a language model; J+ is the writer's hooked 1, the key's untranscribed blocks are nulls ('Nonvaleurs'), and four key slips were read on the key images; both letters now read in full (R1026 0.735, R1027 0.867 clean sentences), four words carried in part and three faint clear-text words open.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b24): both documents of outcome.texts read (2 of 2; 471 of 471 groups by document length, ciphertext_R1026/R1027.txt). Earlier: 0 (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R1026, Berlin, 29 Dec 1787, Van Reede to Van de Spiegel
texts.summary: Van Reede to Van de Spiegel, Berlin, 29 Dec 1787: the two ministers put the alliance project to the King; Hertzberg motivated his own view; a conference this morning; the King will not guarantee the Dutch possessions overseas; article seven struck out as disagreeable to England at Finckenstein's request; Hertzberg made the treaty temporary, twenty years. Clear passage: his audience on Wednesday, the King invites him to dine. Second cipher passage: the conference decided to say only that if the Republic is attacked by a European power the King will furnish the stipulated aid; he could get it stated more clearly if ordered.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b24) on the figures under the Grand Chiffre R1024: DECODE's 'J+' sign is the writer's hooked 1 (J=1 gives a fitting key word at all 77 occurrences, the 21 Sept LM-chosen digits and J=3 do not); the key's null blocks ('Nonvaleurs' 1-50, 331-370, 1201-1250, 2751-2800, 3131-3160, 3621-3660, read on the key images) explain the 'open codes' 1250, 331, 2800, 3160, and 2637 = cependant was mis-numbered 3637 in the key transcription; four key slips read on the key images (54 est, 2142 paroit, 2143 paroitre, 4910 que); five labels corrected on the letter image. Bar marks read as the code's inflection signs. Word check (b24_vr_align.py): every word of the cipher part carried by its groups or their marks; 403 of 1,388 decoded letters rest on the hooked-1 identification, 24 on the five corrected labels. Body 0.735 clean (25/34), explicit holes 0.971. Open: [?soit], [?fournit], [?énonçoit] (writer's slips or bar marks) and three faint words of the clear passage.

texts.label: R1027, Berlin, 4 Mar 1788
texts.summary: Van Reede to Van de Spiegel, Berlin, 4 Mar 1788: news from Russia that Ségur and Cobenzl are dismayed that the Empress has refused the triple alliance; Keller (the Prussian envoy) has no answer and expects none until the Empress hears from Vienna whether the Emperor is resolved on a vigorous attack on the Turks, which decided the Emperor's declaration; the Empress will wait for the courier sent to London before declaring herself on the King's proposals.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b24) as R1026: J+ = 1 at all 24 occurrences, three labels corrected on the image (3089, 1021, 1969), 4910 = que from the key image; names spelt in key syllables (Segur, Cobentzel, Keller). 118 of 601 decoded letters rest on the hooked 1, 15 on the corrected labels. Body 0.867 clean (13/15), explicit holes 0.933. Open: [?decidement] (spelt de-ci-demi-ent).

prior.where: DECODE holds the key (R1024) and plaintext controls R1028/R1029 of the same code; no reading of R1026 or R1027 was found.
